name: Sagunto (Spain)
description: The four red bars of Aragon on yellow.
history: The flag of four red pales on a gold field is one of the symbols of the identity of Sagunto as a people; a faithful copy of the flag granted by James I to the town of Morvedre is displayed in the council chamber. On 15 December 1929 the people of Sagunto again ratified their loyalty to the ensign granted by the Aragonese king, when a flag embroidered as an exact copy of the primitive fourteenth-century one was blessed in the church of Santa María and, as recorded in the minutes of 23 and 30 December 1929, the provincial governor and the council ordered that it should henceforth be the standard borne by the council as the Senyera of the city.
